prompt:
A cinematic storyboard sheet for a Sri Lankan television drama: 3 photorealistic film stills of ONE scene, laid out in a grid 2 panels across and 2 down, read left to right, then top to bottom. Every panel is a tall portrait 9:16 still of the same size, separated by thin, even, plain white gutters. All panels are the same scene's world, painted together: the same people, props, light and colour grade in every panel. The weather and the ground (dry or wet, rain falling or not) are as each panel says: they can change during the scene, and a panel that says it is dry has no rain and no wet ground.

Reference images, in order: image 1 is the location plate for Modern Hotel Operations Office; image 2 is the approved last panel of the previous part of this scene's board. Take from image 1: the kind of place: its ground, water, plants, structures and materials. It is ONE view of the place; each panel has its own camera position, so do not repeat this view in every panel; image 2: panel 1 of this sheet, repeated exactly: the same camera, place, light and mannequins.

People (every panel): every person is a smooth, matte, faceless artist's mannequin in one solid colour, with jointed limbs and simple hands: Company A Operations Manager (Employee) is the red mannequin; Company B Operations Manager is the blue mannequin. A small raised ridge on the front of the head, where a nose would be, shows which way the head faces. Each mannequin has the person's real height and build and sits, stands and holds things exactly as a real person would. No faces, no hair, no clothes, no skin: only the mannequin colour. Everything else (the place, the props, the light, the weather) is a real, photorealistic film still.

World (every panel): Paint one unified storyboard image with four columns and three rows, placing eleven panels in reading order and leaving the bottom-right cell plain and empty. Use smooth, featureless artist's mannequins: Company A Operations Manager (Employee) is red, medium-height and average-built; Company B Operations Manager is blue, medium-tall and lean. Keep their proportions and colours consistent throughout. Render the office and equipment realistically: cream walls, pale oak workstations, flush timber cupboards, dark task chairs, glazed partitions, a matte-black widescreen monitor, compact black keyboard and black mouse. Soft daytime window light comes from the established left side, supplemented by warm recessed lighting; maintain warm-neutral whites, honey-toned timber, restrained saturation and moderate contrast. Conditions remain dry with steady daylight. All interfaces are flat screen graphics with blank fields and unlettered cards. Draw no writing, numerals, logos, captions, panel labels or arrows anywhere.

Geography: The demonstration occupies one workstation in a connected open office. The blue mannequin stands at its west end, screen left facing east; the red mannequin stands at its east end, screen right facing west. The monitor stands between them, angled diagonally toward the southwest audience side. A broad window occupies the northwest background, low oak storage continues along the west wall, and glazed partitions enclose the east side. Every camera remains south of the line between the managers. The opening view looks north across both positions; singles isolate either end, southwest display-side positions reveal the screen, and the final southeast position sees the monitor's back. Neither mannequin changes stations. The northwest window and continuous oak storage establish that these are different views within the same office.

PANEL 1 (row 1, column 1) — Level with the display's status area, near-frontal from the southwest audience side; 85mm macro insert with shallow isolation on the status plane. Background: The white quotation surface fills the panel. Its other content is outside the crop, and the established window remains outside frame left. A large blank amber-outlined status badge is centred against the clean white digital sheet. Its thin amber border is crisp, with generous white space surrounding it. The crop excludes the quotation rows, totals and all people.
PANEL 2 (row 1, column 2) — Return to shot 3's audience-side camera position at standing head height; 50mm waist-up medium shot, with open space on the right. Background: The same pale window edge stays frame left, with softly resolved oak storage behind. The desk corner remains lower right, while the computer display and visitor stay outside the right crop. The blue mannequin stands on the left third with its chest facing right and its head inclined slightly toward the visitor outside the frame. At waist level, one empty hand rests loosely over the other beside the workstation, distinguishing this pose from the earlier single. The computer's screen remains outside the composition.
PANEL 3 (row 2, column 1) — Standing head height from the southeast end of the same audience side, looking northwest; 40mm medium-wide opening frame, blue mannequin visible from mid-thigh upward. Background: The west-wall oak cupboards recede along frame left, while the broad northwest window appears behind and to the upper right of the blue mannequin. The pale oak workstation occupies the lower right, with the monitor's black back facing the camera. The blue mannequin stands screen left, chest facing right and head turned three-quarter toward the visitor beyond the right edge. Both empty hands hang relaxed beside its hips, the near hand clearly visible and the far hand partly concealed by the body. The workstation and the back of the monitor fill the lower-right portion, with the red mannequin entirely outside the frame.

Bodies (every panel): each person sits or stands the way a real person does the task in front of them, never posed for the camera. The body faces the task and only the head turns: someone at a steering wheel sits squarely behind it, the wheel centred in front of the chest, back against the seat, both hands on the rim; someone at a desk sits square to it; someone at a stove faces the stove. A camera beside a person sees the body side-on, not the chest. Nobody looks into or faces the lens unless the panel says so. Head and eyes turn together: the eyes never roll hard to one side while the face points at the camera; a near-frontal face looks just past the lens.

Draw NO text of any kind: no panel numbers, no captions, no titles, no timestamps, no arrows, no labels, no borders other than the gutters. The people, place and everyday details are Sri Lankan.
